correctness.rationale: The directional recurrences are reconstructed from the classical Saul'yev coefficients. For nonnegative beta and gamma, each recurrence preserves the nonnegative orthant, proving sufficiency. For r greater than one, the exact first column of the left sweep is beta^{j-1} gamma, and the bottom row of the right sweep uses only the last two left-sweep values, giving the closed negative corner beta^{n-1} gamma(1+gamma) for every n at least two. The n=1 product is gamma squared. The packaged exact-rational checker independently replays these identities.

value.rationale: The heat equation preserves nonnegative data, while Saul'yev schemes are historically attractive precisely because they remove the explicit Euler stability restriction. The finding gives a complete sharp distinction between unconditional Fourier stability and pointwise physical admissibility for the standard alternating use: a single scalar threshold, an exact negative matrix entry beyond it, and the minimal interior-grid size for failure. The n=1 cancellation also shows that simply observing a negative one-sweep coefficient is insufficient.
